title: Shallow Module
pattern: An empty struct or interface boundary whose public methods contain zero local logic, simply delegating directly to a standard library or collection operation with no signature transformations.
why_bad: It increases the system's interface complexity without hiding any internal complexity (low depth). Callers must learn and maintain a verbose, custom API for a trivial, self-explanatory operation, adding boilerplate and cognitive load without any encapsulation benefit.
detection: An empty `struct` or a module containing functions that have a 1:1 signature and delegation mapping directly to standard library/collection operations with zero additional control flow or transformations.
counterexample: `Context-dependent`. Thin wrappers implementing standard interface traits (like `io::Write` or `Default`) or thin wrappers designed specifically to isolate a volatile external dependency at an API boundary.
fix: Inline the method's behavior at all call sites and delete the shallow helper struct or function. This restores deep interfaces.
source: John K. Ousterhout, *A Philosophy of Software Design* (2018), Chapter 4 ("Modules Should Be Deep"), pp. 25, 290–292.
